text: Compton Medical Centre has billed 56 claims through a single doctor while reporting zero beds and a registration only 0.9 years old; 94.6% of its claims arrive through one feeder broker and 92.9% of its payouts leave into one account. Every patient appears exactly once and never returns - a one-journey share of 100%. Volume without footprint, a single feeder, a single drain, and disposable patients each have innocent versions, but all five together on a brand-new entity is the assembled ghost-clinic pattern. It also shares its registered address with another operation, which fits a paper-entity setup. A genuine new day-surgery could look similar in its first months, though it would usually diversify referral sources faster than this. Next step: verify physical premises and equipment against the claimed procedures, starting with an unannounced records request.
